stemMd: A eukaryotic cell lacks functioning mitochondria but retains cytosolic enzymes and glucose. Which pathway can still directly yield a small amount of ATP?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Oxidative phosphorylation on the inner mitochondrial membrane

options.label: D
options.textMd: The Calvin cycle in a human cell

explanationMd: Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol and makes ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation. Its continuation also requires regeneration of NAD+, but the pathway itself does not require mitochondria.

distractorRationale.d: Human cells have no Calvin cycle.
distractorRationale.a: This requires the appropriate mitochondrial machinery.
distractorRationale.e: These complexes require a functioning mitochondrial system.
